newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: EU, ASEAN agree modest measures to boost trade.
newsitem.headline: EU, ASEAN agree modest measures to boost trade.

text.p: The European Union and the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) agreed on Friday to take a series of steps to boost trade and economic cooperation.

Trade has already quadrupled since 1980 between the 15-member EU -- the world's largest trading entity -- and the seven-member ASEAN, which aims to create its own free trade area by 2003 encompassing a population larger than Europe's.

"The developments taking place in the two regions give us optimism that there is a great potential for a further strengthening of our economic links," said a declaration at the end of a two-day conference of foreign ministers.
In 1995, the value of ASEAN-EU trade reached $86 billion, or four times what it was in 1980 when the two sides first signed an agreement to cement ties.
The declaration said the two regions "would initiate cooperation in customs matters" and arrange common industrial norms and standards.
They would share information on the creation of the Single Market in the European Union and the ASEAN Free Trade Area.
The two sides would take "measures to increase awareness of business opportunities and business environments in both regions and minimise impediments to inter-regional trade".
The 22 foreign ministers "expressed our conviction that further liberalisation of investment conditions would lead to increased investment flows".
They welcomed the developing role of the European Investment Bank in ASEAN countries, which are Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
The ministers agreed to promote programmes aimed at boosting more joint ventures and business ties between the two regions.
The declaration called for increased cooperation in fighting international organised crime, terrorism and drug smuggling and for more exchanges on education between the regions.

Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong, who opened the ASEAN-EU meeting on Thursday, said ASEAN would have a combined population of 500 million consumers and a gross domestic product of $500 billion by the year 2000.
He urged the EU to stop looking at ASEAN as a collection of "tiger" economies posing a competitive threat to Europe and to stop linking human rights to trade privileges.
